name: Animal Policy International: banning low-welfare animal imports into New Zealand (Ambitious Impact, 2022 idea report)
summary: Ambitious Impact's 2022 estimate for a new charity advocating for New Zealand to ban imports of animal products made below its own welfare standards (fish, meat, eggs, milk and wool from countries ranked D or worse on World Animal Protection's index). The idea Animal Policy International was founded to run. A re-implementation of AIM's spreadsheet as it stands today, traced from its welfare points per dollar of charity costs (168; the report gives 186 from an earlier version, and 23 counting the government's enforcement costs), with the discounting over 40 years rebuilt from the yearly rows. Fish are 96% of the welfare points. Welfare points have no exchange rate to the site's scale, so a bridge of ours turns them into days of pain for each species, weighed by Rethink Priorities' welfare ranges. AIM also lists a 3.4% a year chance that New Zealand would pass the ban anyway, but doesn't use it, so the result assumes it never would.

source.title: Ban low-welfare imports (CE 2022 animal welfare report): CEA

sections.title: Costs counted (ours)
sections.explainer: charityevals' step, not Ambitious Impact's. Ambitious Impact reports welfare points per dollar of the charity's costs, and separately per dollar of the charity's and the government's costs (the government pays to enforce the ban). With credit by share of resources on, the government's enforcement costs count as part of the cost, so your dollar gets the charity's share of the outcome.

sections.title: Staff pay below market
sections.explainer: charityevals' step, not Ambitious Impact's: with credit by share of resources on, staff's forgone pay counts as part of the cost.

sections.title: From welfare points to days of pain (ours)
sections.explainer: charityevals' bridge, not Ambitious Impact's. Ambitious Impact's welfare points (used until 2023) count one point of an animal's welfare score (−100 to +100) for one year, times its chance that the animal is sentient. We take the sentience discount out (Rethink Priorities' weights below already include it) and turn each welfare-point-year into days of disabling pain on the animal's own scale (shared figure, with a range).

sections.title: In chicken pain days
sections.explainer: charityevals' species step, the same for every animal model: days of pain for each species, weighed by how much it can suffer relative to a chicken (Rethink Priorities).

rows.label: Discount rate
rows.explainer: Ambitious Impact discounts future costs and welfare points at 0.04 a year. Linked to the shared discount rate (Your values); the evaluator view pins it to Ambitious Impact's rate.

rows.label: Years the reform counts before it would have come anyway
rows.explainer: Changed for consistency: reads the shared "Years a won reform counts before it would have come anyway" (5 by default), like every model that credits a won reform. Ambitious Impact counts a New Zealand ban on low-welfare imports for every year of its sheet once it takes effect, years 6 to 40 (35 years), as if it would never have come otherwise; that span is kept as the evaluator's and used in the evaluator view. The five years until it takes effect and every year counted are discounted at "Next year's good counts less by", as Ambitious Impact's sheet does.

rows.label: % likelihood each year of government passing law without any interventions from animal welfare community
rows.explainer: "Best guess based on an estimate that this would happen in ~20 years without intervention" (AIM, C11). AIM lists this counterfactual but no formula uses it, so AIM's result assumes the ban would never happen without the charity. Our view counts the ban only for the shared "Years a won reform counts before it would have come anyway" (row years_counted) instead, so this row stays for reference and doesn't feed the result.

rows.label: Chicken-equivalent pain days averted per dollar you give: cattle, sheep and goats
rows.explainer: The days of pain for cattle, sheep and goats, weighed by how much cattle can suffer relative to a chicken (Rethink Priorities' pig as the stand-in; we use it for sheep and goats too). The cattle weight is a stand-in, our judgment: Rethink Priorities didn't estimate cattle, sheep or goats, so the pig's weight stands in (facts: welfare_ranges.cattle_vs_chicken, kind judgment).

rows.label: Chicken-equivalent pain days averted per dollar you give
rows.explainer: Days of disabling pain spared, all species, counted as a chicken's. The headline converts this into years of healthy life with the chicken slider and the healthy hours lost per day of disabling pain.
